its distinctive anatomy, clear enough to identify the species (name added as an overlay)

the adult form of the body

shots.narration: This jellyfish may never die of old age.
shots.goal: Introduce the star: one small, healthy jellyfish with a glowing-looking red-orange core, alone in dark water.
shots.action: The jellyfish hangs in the water and pulses its bell in slow, regular contractions, tentacles fanning out after each pulse
shots.composition: jellyfish centred in the upper half of the frame, bell top at about one-third height, tentacles spreading below it
must_show: transparent bell with a red-orange core inside
fringe of fine white tentacles around the bell rim
a single jellyfish
edit_notes: Hook text on frame zero per README rule 1: 'THIS JELLYFISH / MAY NEVER DIE / OF OLD AGE.'

shots.goal: Show the anatomy that identifies the species: clear bell, red-orange core, tentacle fringe, seen from the side.
shots.action: The jellyfish pulses once as the camera circles from the front to a side view of the bell
shots.composition: bell in profile in the upper half, core clearly inside the bell, tentacles hanging below
must_show: bell shape and tentacle fringe clearly readable
red-orange core inside the bell
fine white tentacles
edit_notes: Overlay the species name 'Turritopsis dohrnii' in the edit; never generate it
must_happen: the camera circles to a side view of the bell

shots.narration: and it's smaller than your pinky nail.
shots.goal: Scale: the whole jellyfish is visibly smaller than the fingernail beside it.
shots.environment: one dish in close view, the jellyfish floating in it
shots.action: The fingertip holds still in the water just beside the jellyfish while the jellyfish pulses gently
shots.composition: fingertip entering from the upper right, jellyfish just left of centre, both fully in frame at the same focus distance
must_show: fingernail and jellyfish side by side in one frame
the whole jellyfish smaller than the fingernail
must_avoid: jellyfish as large as or larger than the fingertip
accuracy_notes: Scale must read correctly: adult bell ~4.5 mm, a pinky nail ~8-10 mm wide

shots.narration: When it's injured, starving, or under extreme stress,
shots.goal: The same adult, now plainly damaged and weak.
shots.action: The damaged jellyfish pulses weakly and unevenly, sinking slightly between pulses, broken tentacle pieces drifting away from it
shots.composition: jellyfish centred in the upper half, torn side of the bell facing the camera
must_show: torn, notched bell rim
missing or broken tentacles
red-orange core still visible

shots.narration: it can transform its adult body back
shots.goal: The adult body visibly shrinking and folding in on itself.
shots.action: The bell contracts and folds inward while the tentacles shorten and are drawn up toward the body; the whole animal shrinks to about half its size
shots.composition: subject held in the same place in the frame from start to end so the shrinking is obvious
must_show: the bell folding inward
tentacles getting shorter
overall size clearly smaller by the end
must_avoid: the jellyfish exploding or dissolving into particles
sudden cut or pop between sizes
accuracy_notes: Real process takes hours; shown as a time-lapse
edit_notes: Optional subtle 'rewind' speed ramp in the edit; no text needed

shots.narration: into an earlier stage of its life cycle.
shots.goal: Reveal the earlier life stage it is heading back to: a colony of tiny polyps anchored to rock.
shots.action: The polyps' tentacle crowns sway gently in a slow current while the camera moves closer
shots.composition: polyp colony across the middle of the frame, rock below, dark water above
must_show: several upright polyps with crowns of fine white tentacles
thin tubes linking the polyps on the rock
reddish colour in the polyps matching the adult's core
edit_notes: Optional overlay 'POLYP = ITS BABY FORM' only if the test audience misreads it; the narration after this explains it

shots.narration: It sinks, absorbs its own tentacles,
shots.goal: The shrunken jellyfish sinking onto the rock while its tentacles disappear into its body.
shots.action: The shrunken body drifts downward and settles on the rock; the last tentacle stubs retract into it as it lands
shots.movement_note: follows the body down to the rock
shots.composition: starts with the body high in frame and ends with it resting on the rock surface in the lower-middle
must_show: the body moving downward
landing on the rock
tentacles retracting into the body
accuracy_notes: Continues the S05 state (reverting); S06 is a cutaway to where it is heading

shots.narration: and collapses into a tiny blob.
shots.goal: The body loses every jellyfish feature and becomes a small round blob stuck to the rock.
shots.action: The rounded body slumps and smooths out into a small featureless ball with a thin translucent skin
shots.composition: blob centred in the frame on the rock surface
must_show: a small round featureless blob on the rock
red-orange interior visible through a thin clear skin
no bell and no tentacles by the end
accuracy_notes: The cyst stage has no recognisable medusa or polyp features (Matsumoto et al. 2019)

shots.narration: Within a few days, that blob sprouts into polyps —
shots.goal: Time-lapse: the blob sends out root-like tubes and a first polyp grows upward.
shots.environment: sediment particles shifting slightly between frames as in a time-lapse
shots.action: Thin translucent tubes creep outward from the blob across the rock and a tiny polyp bud grows upright from them
shots.composition: blob starts centred; the pull-out leaves room for the tubes spreading to the frame edges
must_show: the same blob at the start
tubes growing out across the rock
an upright polyp bud by the end
accuracy_notes: Cyst develops stolons and polyps within about 24-36 hours; compressed to seconds

shots.narration: the jellyfish's baby form — which bud off brand-new jellyfish.
shots.goal: The polyp colony, and a brand-new tiny jellyfish pulling free from a polyp and swimming off.
shots.action: Polyps sway on their stalks; on the side of one polyp a tiny bell pulses, pulls free and swims upward out of the colony
shots.movement_note: follows the new jellyfish upward at the end
shots.composition: colony in the lower half; the new jellyfish rises into the upper half
must_show: polyps with tentacle crowns
a tiny bell forming on the side of one polyp
red-orange core in the tiny bell
must_happen: the tiny new jellyfish pulls free from the polyp and swims upward

shots.narration: They're genetic copies of the original.
shots.goal: Several new jellyfish that look exactly like each other, framed exactly like the opening shot of the original.
shots.action: Three young jellyfish pulse in unison, side by side, as the camera pans across them
shots.composition: the three jellyfish in a loose horizontal row in the upper half, same spacing, same size
must_show: three jellyfish with matching size, shape and red-orange cores
the same look as the S01 adult
must_avoid: jellyfish of different species or colours
one visibly larger than the others
edit_notes: Match-cut to S01's framing so the likeness is obvious

shots.narration: In the lab, they've reset again and again.
shots.goal: A row of lab dishes showing the cycle stages side by side: this has been watched happening repeatedly.
shots.environment: three dishes in a row: the nearest holds an adult jellyfish, the middle one a small round blob, the farthest a polyp colony
shots.action: Focus moves from the jellyfish in the nearest dish to the blob in the middle dish and on to the polyps in the farthest dish
shots.composition: dishes running diagonally from lower-left (near) to upper-right (far)
must_show: three glass culture dishes
an adult jellyfish in one dish
a blob in another dish
a polyp colony in another dish
must_avoid: legible labels or text on the dishes
accuracy_notes: Repeated reversal is from lab rearing observations; the three dishes show stages, not one animal at once

shots.narration: In the wild, most still get eaten.
shots.goal: Back in open water, a small fish darts in and swallows the jellyfish.
shots.action: A small silver fish swims in from the left toward the pulsing jellyfish, opens its mouth, swallows the jellyfish in one bite and turns away
shots.composition: jellyfish in the upper-middle; the fish close to it at the left edge, mouth open
must_show: the jellyfish in open water
a small fish close to it with its mouth open
accuracy_notes: Predators include fish; generic small fish chosen, not a specific documented predator species
must_happen: the fish swallows the jellyfish in one bite
the jellyfish is gone after the bite
